sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `kimi-code`
- Canonical name: Kimi Code (service) / Kimi Code CLI (runtime) (`claim-kimi-code-sf-identity`). Historical nw identity is **Kimi CLI** (`claim-kimi-code-nw-identity`).
- Current status: generally available; CLI actively released (`claim-kimi-code-sf-status`). Historical nw mixed published (`claim-kimi-code-nw-status-published`) and winding-down (`claim-kimi-code-nw-status-wind-down`).
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-17
- Vendor: Moonshot AI (`claim-kimi-code-sf-vendor`, `claim-kimi-code-nw-vendor`)
- Canonical URL: https://www.kimi.com/code/ (`claim-kimi-code-sf-canonical-url`). Historical nw github.io/kimi-cli (`claim-kimi-code-nw-canonical-url`).
- Repository: https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code (`claim-kimi-code-sf-repository-url`). Historical nw MoonshotAI/kimi-cli (`claim-kimi-code-nw-repository-url`).
- Version: **0.36.1 (2026-08-14)** (`claim-kimi-code-sf-version`). Historical nw kimi-cli 1.49.0 (`claim-kimi-code-nw-version`).
- Availability: public install; model tiers gated (`claim-kimi-code-sf-availability`). Historical nw (`claim-kimi-code-nw-availability`).

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: intelligent programming service in Kimi membership; CLI/VS Code agent that reads/edits code, runs commands, and plans (`claim-kimi-code-sf-identity`, `claim-kimi-code-sf-unique-value`). Historical nw: terminal coding agent (`claim-kimi-code-nw-what-it-is`).

- What it is not: not Kimi Platform pay-as-you-go API; not Kimi Claw; not consumer Kimi Get App (`claim-kimi-code-sf-not-for`). Historical nw not-for-cloud is unknown (`claim-kimi-code-nw-not-for-cloud`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: runtime (`claim-kimi-code-sf-primary-type`, `claim-kimi-code-nw-primary-type`). Inference from local agent-core-v2 owning the loop. Must stay runtime.

- Agent-loop owner: local Kimi Code runtime / agent-core-v2 on TUI, kimi -p, kimi acp (`claim-kimi-code-sf-agent-loop-owner`). Historical nw: kimi-cli owns the loop (`claim-kimi-code-nw-agent-loop-owner`).

- Architecture: local main Agent + agent-core-v2; remote HTTP models; optional kimi web (`claim-kimi-code-sf-architecture`). Historical nw Kosong/PyKAOS/Wire/Rust (`claim-kimi-code-nw-architecture-kosong`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface ledger rows were not written this pass. Prose surfaces: CLI TUI, kimi -p, VS Code, ACP, kimi web, membership coding API (`claim-kimi-code-sf-surface`, `claim-kimi-code-sf-access-route`).

- Historical nw also recorded VS Code Node SDK (`claim-kimi-code-nw-surface-vscode-listing`) and legacy Toad/Zsh (`claim-kimi-code-nw-surface-term`, `claim-kimi-code-nw-surface-zsh`).

- Execution location: local CLI / VS Code Extension Host; model inference remote (`claim-kimi-code-sf-execution-location`). Historical nw: same-device local (`claim-kimi-code-nw-execution-local`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: official IDs k3, k3-256k, kimi-for-coding, kimi-for-coding-highspeed plus providers (`claim-kimi-code-sf-model-strategy`).

- Auth: Kimi Code OAuth and/or operator API keys (`claim-kimi-code-sf-auth-strategy`). Contradicts nw env-override (`claim-kimi-code-nw-auth-env-override`).

- Providers: kimi, anthropic, openai, openai_responses, google-genai, vertexai (`claim-kimi-code-sf-provider-support`).

- BYOK: supported (`claim-kimi-code-sf-byok`). Subscription reuse: unknown (`claim-kimi-code-sf-subscription-reuse`). Local models: not written (no first-party local-models sentence). Historical nw local-models row is provider_support unknown (`claim-kimi-code-nw-local-models`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context: k3 up to 1M (Allegretto+); others 256k (`claim-kimi-code-sf-context-behavior`).

- Memory: session logs + AGENTS.md / skills (`claim-kimi-code-sf-memory`). Historical nw: AGENTS.md plus stored sessions (`claim-kimi-code-nw-memory`).

- Compaction: auto near window; /compact (`claim-kimi-code-sf-compaction`, `claim-kimi-code-nw-compaction`).

- Session: persist, continue, fork, export (`claim-kimi-code-sf-session-behavior`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: built-in file/shell/web/plan/agent/swarm/cron (`claim-kimi-code-sf-tools`). Historical nw tool list is kimi-cli-era (`claim-kimi-code-nw-tools`).

- Extensions: plugins, ACP, VS Code (`claim-kimi-code-sf-extensions`).

- MCP: client stdio/HTTP/SSE (`claim-kimi-code-sf-mcp`). Skills: SKILL.md scopes (`claim-kimi-code-sf-skills`). Hooks: fail-open (`claim-kimi-code-sf-hooks`).

- APIs: membership coding API plus local kimi web REST/WS (`claim-kimi-code-sf-api`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: main agent + coder/explore/plan + swarm (`claim-kimi-code-sf-orchestration`). Historical nw also recorded Ralph (`claim-kimi-code-nw-orchestration-ralph`) as a kimi-cli-era row.

- Parallelism: parallel sub-agents; AgentSwarm up to 128 (`claim-kimi-code-sf-parallelism`, `claim-kimi-code-nw-parallelism`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: permissions/trust/sub-agent context only. No OS sandbox for Code. Do not use Claw sandbox (`claim-kimi-code-sf-isolation`). Historical nw isolation unknown (`claim-kimi-code-nw-isolation`).

- Permissions: approval panel; YOLO/Auto/Plan (`claim-kimi-code-sf-permissions`).

- Security: trust prompt, binary-planting fixes, web token/password (`claim-kimi-code-sf-security`).

- Data path: ~/.kimi-code/ (`claim-kimi-code-sf-data-path`). Historical nw ~/.kimi (`claim-kimi-code-nw-data-path`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Surfaces in prose only; not surfaces.jsonl IDs (`claim-kimi-code-sf-surface`).

- Remote: self-hosted kimi web --host; default loopback (`claim-kimi-code-sf-remote-access`). Historical nw remote_access unknown (`claim-kimi-code-nw-remote-access`).

- Mobile: unsupported. No official Code iOS/Android app (`claim-kimi-code-sf-mobile`, `claim-kimi-code-sf-mobile-access`). Historical nw mobile_access unknown (`claim-kimi-code-nw-mobile-access`).

- Background: Ctrl+B, /tasks, cron (`claim-kimi-code-sf-background`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Kimi membership Moderato $19 / Allegretto $39 / Allegro $99 / Vivace $199 per month (`claim-kimi-code-sf-pricing`). Historical nw prices unknown (`claim-kimi-code-nw-pricing`). Do not claim harness $0 as product price.

- License: CLI MIT (`claim-kimi-code-sf-license`). Marketplace listing Apache-2.0 (`claim-kimi-code-sf-license-marketplace`). Historical nw kimi-cli Apache-2.0 (`claim-kimi-code-nw-license`). Do not average.

- Maintenance: through 0.36.1 (2026-08-14) (`claim-kimi-code-sf-maintenance`). No stars.

- Lock-in: official Kimi models need membership; operator keys documented (`claim-kimi-code-sf-byok`, `claim-kimi-code-sf-drawback`).

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage: kimi-cli Python/uv ~/.kimi to Kimi Code CLI Node/TS ~/.kimi-code; kimi migrate (`claim-kimi-code-sf-lineage`). Historical nw already pointed at successor repo (`claim-kimi-code-nw-lineage-kimi-code`).

- Relationship edges: none written this pass.

- Compatibility: coding API into Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex; ACP Zed/JetBrains (`claim-kimi-code-sf-compatibility`).

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison-neighborhood ledger rows were not written this pass.

- Same-lineage: legacy kimi-cli is this catalogue identity, not a second product (`claim-kimi-code-sf-lineage`, `claim-kimi-code-nw-identity-same-product-renamed`, `claim-kimi-code-nw-identity-successor-separate`).

- Often-confused: Kimi Platform; Kimi Claw; consumer Kimi Get App (`claim-kimi-code-sf-not-for`).

- Substitutes / partials / complements: unknown.

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: local MIT runtime + official Kimi membership models; 1M K3; ACP; swarm; MCP/skills/hooks (`claim-kimi-code-sf-unique-value`).

- Drawbacks: membership/quota; no OS sandbox; hooks fail-open; do not dual-open CLI+VS Code (`claim-kimi-code-sf-drawback`).

- Best fit: developers wanting terminal/IDE agent programming (`claim-kimi-code-sf-intended-user`).

- Not-for: Kimi Platform embedding; official mobile Code app (`claim-kimi-code-sf-not-for`).

sections.heading: Research note on pre-existing ledger rows
sections.body: `claim-kimi-code-nw-*` rows (105 claims, captured 2026-08-16) were not deleted or rewritten. This pass appends only `claim-kimi-code-sf-*`. No stars claim. No `field=local_models` row. No generate-site-data run. Surface ledger rows were not written this pass.

claims.claim: Configuration exposes loop_control with max_steps_per_turn, max_retries_per_step, max_ralph_iterations, reserved_context_size, and compaction_trigger_ratio, showing the CLI runs and bounds its own agent loop.
kimi acp starts a multi-session ACP server for IDE plugins and custom clients and returns AUTH_REQUIRED when the user has not logged in.
Print mode runs non-interactively with text or stream-json input and output and an option to emit only the final assistant message.
claims.notes: --print implies away-from-keyboard behavior, which bypasses approval prompts rather than adding an approval feature.

claims.claim: Wire mode exposes a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdin and stdout for building custom UIs, embedding the agent, or automated testing.
claims.notes: Marked experimental on the command reference.

claims.claim: The repository bundles PyKAOS, an OS abstraction whose file and command operations can switch between the local environment and remote systems over SSH.
claims.notes: Library capability; the CLI's own remote support is limited, see execution-local.

claims.claim: The repository bundles Kosong, an LLM abstraction layer that unifies message structures, asynchronous tool orchestration, and pluggable chat providers.
claims.notes: Declared as a dependency in pyproject.toml.

claims.claim: Wire-mode docs describe a separate Rust Kimi Agent binary that is wire-mode only, supports the Kimi provider only, has no account login, and is local execution only with no SSH KAOS support.
claims.notes: Separate repository; recorded as architecture context, not as this product's surface.

claims.claim: Wire is the internal message-passing layer: the shell UI and the ACP server both talk to the agent core through it, and --wire exposes that JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol (version 1.10) over stdin and stdout.
The FAQ warns that KIMI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY environment variables can override the key stored in the config file.
Getting Started says /login recommends the Kimi Code platform, which opens a browser for OAuth authorization, while other platforms need an API key.
claims.value: OAuth for Kimi Code; API keys elsewhere
claims.notes: kimi login and kimi logout manage the same credentials.

claims.claim: Install is a one-line script for Linux and macOS or a PowerShell command on Windows, or uv tool install; Python 3.12 to 3.14 is supported with 3.13 recommended.
The agent can launch long-running commands as background tasks that return a task id immediately, and when a task finishes while the agent is idle the system triggers a new turn to process results.
claims.value: background shell tasks with completion callback
claims.notes: /task manages them; keep_alive_on_exit is configurable.

claims.claim: Repository metadata lists https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-cli/ as the project homepage.
The CLI compresses context automatically when needed, and /compact summarizes the conversation and replaces the context, optionally with instructions about what to keep.
claims.notes: A status bar shows context usage in tokens.

claims.claim: System prompts receive built-in variables including merged AGENTS.md content from the project root to the working directory, the working-directory listing, the loaded skills list, and added directories.
claims.notes: /init generates AGENTS.md when a project lacks one.

claims.claim: Each model declares max_context_size, and loop_control sets reserved_context_size (default 50000) and compaction_trigger_ratio (default 0.85).
claims.value: configurable context budget and compaction trigger

claims.claim: Local state lives under ~/.kimi: config.toml, mcp.json, MCP OAuth tokens, logs at ~/.kimi/logs/kimi.log, and session directories including subagent history.
The FAQ says cd in shell mode does not change the working directory because each command runs in its own subprocess.
claims.value: no persistent cd in shell mode

claims.claim: The project is documented as winding down, with new users encouraged to install the successor instead.
claims.value: successor product recommended for new users
claims.notes: Docs tip repeats the README notice.

claims.claim: Opened first-party pages document no enterprise plan, SSO, or team-administration capability for this CLI.
claims.notes: Repair: reviewer listed enterprise, SSO and team administration as uncovered. Absence on the opened pages, not a denial that such features exist.

claims.claim: Agent tools act on the working directory given by --work-dir plus directories added with --add-dir, and shell commands run as local subprocesses.
